name: score
title: Score
description: The score a player reads, as a thin wrapper over `stat`: every number, typeface, tabular numeral and state word is stat's, and score adds one thing, the count from the old number to the new one. `data-gs-value` carries the settled number from the moment the host gives it and `data-gs-counting` says only that the text on screen has not caught up, so an interrupted count, a suppressed one and a finished one all report the same truth. Reduced motion has no count-up at all: the number is correct at once. The accessible name holds the settled number throughout, never the one the animation is passing through. It fixes `kind="score"` so the host does not have to remember the kind, and its root carries `data-gs-component="score"` so a test can find it beside the timer and round. The count is presentation: it does not award points, fetch a score or settle the number. Use plain `stat` when the host chooses the kind at runtime or wants a score rendered without the count-up or a separate score root. Draws as the ringed chip the design draws, rather than as a label above a bare number; pass presentation to change the silhouette.
docs: Pass `value` and re-render with a new one; the change counts up. Pass `countUp={false}` when the score is being restored rather than earned, and it lands at once. The count's duration is the `--gs-motion-fill` token, which is 0ms under reduced motion, so reduced motion needs nothing from the host. Read `data-gs-value` for the number and never the rendered text: mid-count they differ, which is the point.
